The shared concept bridging these clusters is the idea that human faculties—whether sensory perception of the divine or cognitive capacities like self-awareness and rationality—are not intrinsic or emergent from physical matter, but are instead externally supplied or influenced by non-human, spiritual entities. Both clusters characterize human cognition and spiritual experience as dependent on an external, often divine source, vulnerable to distortion or granted as gifts. This positions human nature as fundamentally receptive to a transcendent agency rather than autonomously emergent.

**Conclusion:** Extrinsic spiritual causation of human cognition and perception.
